verdict.reasoning: Patient says he has been feeling unwell with cough and cold for a few days: "I haven't been feeling well, for, a good few days" and later dates onset to Saturday, about "four, five days ago".

He describes: "mostly, dry... a wee bit in the morning it's a bit worse" and then agrees to phlegm: Doctor: "So you're not bringing up any mucky, flem?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah... It's a wee bit, wee bit uh, yeah."

Runny nose: Doctor: "bit of a runny nose, you mentioned" Patient: "Yeah, yeah, yeah". Sore throat and hoarse from shouting at football: Patient: "I've had a bit of a sore throat... I'm doing a lot of...watching the football... So I've been, shouting myself a wee bit hoarse."

He reports shortness of breath without chest pain: Doctor: "you're feeling more short of breath?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah." and later, "any pain in your chest at all?" Patient: "No, no... it's just a wee bit shortness of breath... it's not pain."

Feverish/night sweats and blankets: "having to, you know get out and, get the blanket off, and put it back on again". No measured temperature: Patient: "I haven't, haven't, you know, used a thermometer or anything."
He reports transient diarrhea at onset: "the first day I had, you know a wee bit... a wee bit of diarrhoea... but that, that's, that's fine, now."

Generalized myalgias/joint stiffness: Patient: "it's just been a wee... when I'm bending down and... moving about, it's just, a wee, a wee bit stiffer" and to location: "when you're bending like, elbows and knees and just, just a wee bit, kinda stiff"; doctor summarizes "all over".
Appetite and fluids are okay: Patient: "my appetite's been, been all right yeah, yeah. I'm trying to, trying to keep, keep the fluids up as well."
Patient states: "I've got the uh, I've got the diabetes." When asked type: Doctor: "is it type one or type two?" Patient: "it's, it's uh, type, two, two."

He reports previously high blood pressure: "when I was speaking to... another doctor... he took my blood pressure and that said that was, that was high" and doctor clarifies: "You've been diagnosed with high blood pressure".
He describes being overweight: "I'm a wee bit, on the chunky side... I've got a wee bit round the midriff, the spare tyre's, definitely there."
Medication list: Patient: "it's... Metformin?" Doctor: "that's correct."
He lists Lisinopril: Patient: "and there's another one, Lisinopril?" Doctor: "Lisinopril, yeah."
Intermittent aspirin use: Patient: "just those two. Yeah, I mean a wee bit of like, a wee bit of Aspirin or whatever every now and again, but you know nothing long-term."
No known drug allergies: Patient: "not that I'm aware of" and when clarified about medications: "No, nothing, nothing that I'm aware of, doctor's never said nothing to me."

Lives with wife: Doctor: "you said you live, with your wife" and later, "now it's just me and the missus". Work: "there's a wee factory, just down the road... we just manufacture like... kind of steel, steel parts."
Alcohol intake: Patient: "maybe what like four, four pints on like Saturday and then... Sunday as well... maybe like. Nine, nine pints in a week, I would say."

He smokes but is cutting down and vaping: "a wee, every now and again, but I'm, I am trying to cut that down. I've got a wee... vaporisers... I've been cutting down on the cigarettes... got myself one of those."
Children left home: Doctor: "Anyone else at home with you?" Patient: "no, no, kids, the kids have uh, they've flown the nest. So uh, now it's just me and the missus."
Doctor’s assessment: "what you essentially have is a bit of a, a bit of a viral illness perhaps, a bit of a, maybe early signs of a flu"—consistent with viral URI/influenza-like illness.
Type 2 diabetes on Metformin is documented: Patient: "it's, it's uh, type, two" and medications include "Metformin".
Hypertension on Lisinopril: doctor notes diagnosis of high blood pressure and medication list includes "Lisinopril".
Tobacco use and vaping are described: Patient smokes "a wee, every now and again" and is "trying to cut that down" with a "wee... vaporiser."
He self-describes as overweight: "I'm a wee bit, on the chunky side... spare tyre's, definitely there."
Doctor’s advice: "stay rested, drink plenty of fluids" and patient repeats "plenty of rest, lots of water."
Paracetamol recommended: "if you are feeling hot and cold and sweaty, taking regular Paracetamol would be beneficial."

Delayed antibiotics plan: "what we could think about is giving you a script for antibiotics, which maybe use in next, twenty four to forty eight hours, if your symptoms don't get better" and later specifies "something like Amoxicillin. One tablet, three times a day."
The transcript confirms current Metformin and Lisinopril use but does not include any explicit instruction to continue these medications in the plan.

Doctor encourages smoking cessation and supports ongoing efforts: "I wish you all the best on your journey to quit, I highly recommend it. Um, if you can, it'll certainly help your health as well" in response to his vaping to cut down cigarettes.
Although alcohol use is discussed, there is no explicit advice or plan in the transcript instructing the patient to continue moderating alcohol intake.
Follow-up advice: "if you're still not better by next week, come back and see me, we can have another look."
